feature_contract.goal: Reduce full-span CPU depth-signature scanning for large sparse indexed world-particle buffers while retaining identical ascending first-512 world-versus-HUD classification and binocular protected rendering.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only R30 depth-signature read selection; preserve vertex XYZ/RHW writes, both-eye geometry, HUD scope, menu/F11, world shader, SkyGlow, FFB, DX11 and DXVK.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: R30 original fast touched sample was capped at 512 references; a >512 touched count forced one mask visit for every vertex in large VB index windows. A bounded 513-2048 unique sparse list sorted once yields the exact first 512 selected vertices without the often much larger O(vertexCount) scan. No Quest3 frame-time or FPS uplift has yet been measured.
trace_stages: Original OutRun indexed-UP/VB render producers supply selected index masks and touched-list alongside source vertex range.
R30 per-draw projected-depth classifier resolves the first 512 valid selected indices in original ascending order to decide world particle vs HUD.
R30 world/flat-effects per-eye routing and safe D3D9 original draw fallback are unaffected by equivalent depth classification.
subcomponents: Preserve existing direct small sparse path and use a bounded sorted path for large sparse producer-owned masks, never for dense draws.
Reject duplicate, out-of-range, non-mask or allocation-failed sorted hints before classification with original dense fallback.
Extend deterministic HUD/world/invalid parity and destructive negative regression guards in exact-SHA DX9Ex Active policy CI.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: 513-2048 sparse selected vertices avoid full-span iteration while preserving ascending first-512 projected depth classification in both stereo eyes.
Existing <=512 unique direct lists and dense indexed buffers are unchanged; invalid or duplicated large hints use the original dense mask scan.
Destructive mutation and differential parity smoke plus exact SHA Win32 DX9Ex game/host/package and Domain Isolation complete successfully.

diagnosis.original_evidence: Original R30 source switches to dense [0,vertexCount) traversal for >512 touched references, even when most vertices are not referenced by the current draw.
diagnosis.root_cause: Depth classifier only optimized small producer touched lists; full sparse 513-2048 counts were rejected despite exact mask/index provenance.
source_trace: Indexed game Draw publishes touched indices and usedMask.
R30HasProjectedDepthSignature samples an ordered first-512 valid subset.
R30Stereo per-eye read reuses classifier result or original D3D9 fallback.
alternatives_rejected: Unsorted >512 touched order can change the original first-512 world/HUD decision.
Copying every source vertex or enlarging the low-count fast path risks protected per-eye geometry.
Dense draw lists do not justify heap/sort overhead and must use the original scan.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Bounded sorted unique/index membership path with heap-allocation failure fallback and identical ascending first-512 sampling.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Local contract source guard and randomized reference-mask parity with order reversal, duplicate-hint negative cases plus destructive guard mutations.

performance_evidence: Source-level reduction in mask probes for large sparse VB windows only; no hardware FPS asserted.
